tools.name: search_laws
tools.description:
Find the AI-law rules (EU AI Act, US state AI laws, China, Korea and other markets) that apply to an AI feature
in a market, each with its cited provision and official link.

When to use: someone asks which laws, regulations or standards apply to what they are building, or where a kind of
AI feature

tools.name: explain_rule
tools.description:
One rule in plain terms: what it requires (TwinEthos's summary), who it applies to and the uses it excludes, its
dates, the exact citations with their official links, and the guard to add in one sentence (a guard is the change
to make in the application's code or settings, such as a notice, a check

tools.name: plan_guards
tools.description:
The few guards that address the most rules for these AI features and markets, ranked: each guard in one sentence
(a guard is a change to make in the application's code or settings, such as a notice, a check or a human review
step), how many rules it addresses by lane, where binding law on it applies

tools.name: coming_into_force
tools.description:
Binding AI-law obligations that start applying soon, soonest first, with citation, official link and the guard
in one sentence.

When to use: someone asks what is coming, what to prepare for, or which AI laws take effect next year. For dates
already passed, use recently_in_force. Features and market

tools.name: recently_in_force
tools.description:
Binding AI-law obligations that started applying recently, newest first, with citation, official link and the
guard in one sentence.

When to use: someone asks what took effect recently, when the most recent AI law in a market started applying, or
what changed this year. For dates ahead, use coming_

findings.title: Tool description changed since last scan
findings.detail: Tool "search_laws" changed its description with no version change. Silent description changes are how a trusted server turns malicious after review.
